To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
temperament dispositions are linked to basic motivational systems and to the Big Five personality dimensions.

the study of temperament and personality can benefit from a developmental perspective, and that temperament and personality are linked through basic motivational and attentional processes that are supported by biology.

temperament is a set of individual differences in reactivity and self regulation that are present from infancy and that are linked to biological and social processes that support the development of personality and social competence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of personality and temperament in the context of person environment interactions.
the origins and outcomes of personality and temperament in the context of the developing person.
the origins and consequences of individual differences in the basic motivational systems that underlie temperament and personality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
temperament is a critical component of personality.
the temperament approach has much potential to contribute to a better understanding of the development of personality and its relation to social and emotional development.
temperament is an important part of the story of personality, but that the full story is not yet known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a temperament perspective provides a useful way to integrate research across the subdisciplines and to link research across the life span.

temperament is the study of individual differences in basic motivational and affective systems, and personality is the study of the organization and integration of these systems in the context of social and environmental factors.
temperament is a set of basic affective and self regulatory systems that have their origins in biology and development and are linked to the emergence of personality in adulthood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
temperament and personality are not distinct constructs, but are best understood as part of a developmental system.
temperament research provides a unique perspective for understanding how basic biological processes are linked to personality and social functioning.

the integration of biological, developmental, and personality perspectives can help us to understand how temperament dispositions are shaped by biological processes and social experiences, and how they in turn shape adult personality.
